title: When the Songbook Turns
premise: Quentin Voss, a ghostwriter drowning in other people's stories, takes an anonymous pen-pal assignment to pay off his debts—only to discover the stranger on the other end is Marguerite Hale, the rival memoirist whose book he's secretly writing and whose career he once helped destroy. As their letters deepen into love, Quentin must choose between the contract that keeps him solvent and the woman who deserves the truth. When Marguerite uncovers his double betrayal, she publishes her own memoir with his letters woven through it, forcing both of them to forgive themselves before they can forgive each other; they meet at last in a small coastal record shop, choosing each other over the careers that made them enemies.
about_author: Silas Dravenmoor is the pseudonym of a former music journalist who spent a decade writing liner notes for artists who never learned his name. He lives near the sea, where he claims all good second chances wash ashore eventually.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Margins
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. He finishes ghostwriting chapter twelve of Marguerite Hale's memoir and mails off an application for an anonymous pen-pal service he can't afford to refuse. The beat: loneliness disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: Assignment: Stranger
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She accepts the same pen-pal program as research for her book's final chapters, craving one honest voice untouched by her fame. The beat: hope wrapped in cynicism.

chapters.title: First Letter, No Names
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Their first anonymous letters arrive—hers sharp and funny, his disarmingly honest about failure. Neither knows the other's identity. The beat: the electric risk of being seen.

chapters.title: The Rival Across the Table
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. At a publishing gala, Quentin and Marguerite trade public barbs while privately comparing everyone present to their unknown correspondents. The beat: dramatic irony tightening like wire.

chapters.title: What the Sea Keeps
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She writes her pen pal about the coastal town where she grew up and the songbook her mother left behind—the emotional core she refuses to put in her memoir. The beat: guarded tenderness.

chapters.title: Deadlines and Double Lives
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. His editor demands the finished manuscript in six weeks while his pen pal's letters make him feel like a fraud twice over. He starts falling for two versions of the same woman without knowing it. The beat: compounding guilt.

chapters.title: A Song Only Half-Remembered
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Her pen pal quotes a lyric from her mother's songbook—a song she never told anyone outside her family. Suspicion flickers. The beat: the first crack in anonymity.

chapters.title: The Confession He Didn't Send
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin drafts a letter revealing everything, then burns it when his publisher threatens legal action over any breach of the ghostwriting contract. The beat: duty strangling honesty.

chapters.title: Champagne and Almosts
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Forced together by a joint interview, Quentin and Marguerite share a rain-soaked taxi and nearly kiss, each feeling they're betraying someone unseen. The beat: longing at war with loyalty.

chapters.title: Handwriting Like a Hook
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Reviewing old correspondence, Marguerite notices her pen pal's phrasing echoes lines from her own unpublished manuscript pages only her ghostwriter has seen. The beat: dread blooming beneath romance.

chapters.title: The Test Letter
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Marguerite plants a false detail in her next letter; Quentin repeats it verbatim in a manuscript meeting. She now knows—but says nothing, wanting to see how deep the deception runs. The beat: heartbreak weaponized into patience.

chapters.title: Everything I Wrote Was True
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin realizes the trap he's walked into and that his feelings are real regardless of how they began. He decides to confess publicly at her book launch. The beat: resolve born of shame.

chapters.title: Launch Night
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Before Quentin can speak, Marguerite takes the podium and reads one of his letters aloud, unmasking him before three hundred people. The beat: public devastation, private relief that the lie is dead.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Empty Rooms
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Contract terminated, reputation ruined, Quentin returns to his bare apartment and confronts the man in the mirror—the father who taught him invisibility was survival. The beat: rock bottom as beginning.

chapters.title: The Chapter She Cut
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite rereads the memoir chapters Quentin wrote and finds he understood her more truly than anyone ever had—including the parts she'd hidden from herself. The beat: grief complicated by gratitude.

chapters.title: Letters to No One
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Each keeps writing letters to the other, unsent, stacking up like unanswered prayers. A mutual friend quietly begins carrying messages between them. The beat: love persisting past pride.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Offered a lucrative contract to expose Marguerite's family secrets, Quentin refuses—and finally forgives himself for the choices poverty forced on him. The beat: redemption earned, not granted.

chapters.title: What She Published
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite releases a new edition of her memoir with Quentin's letters included under his real name, giving him back his authorship. The beat: restitution as the truest apology.

chapters.title: The Record Shop on Harbor Street
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Following the memoir's final line, Quentin finds Marguerite in the coastal shop where her mother's songbook was printed. They speak plainly for the first time. The beat: truth as homecoming.

chapters.title: Forgiving the Mirror
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin tells Marguerite he can't ask forgiveness until he stops hating himself; she answers that she already did the harder work first. The beat: vulnerability met with grace.

chapters.title: Duet
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Together they finish the song her mother never completed, Marguerite setting words, Quentin setting melody. The beat: collaboration as consummation.

chapters.title: When the Songbook Turns
chapters.summary: Both POVs. One year later, their co-written novel launches—not ghostwritten, not anonymous, two names on the cover. In the acknowledgments, Quentin thanks 'the stranger who was never a stranger.' The beat: belonging, fully chosen.
